questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The principal river of the Kashmir Valley is:
questions.explanation: The Jhelum is the principal river of the Kashmir Valley, rising at Verinag spring in Anantnag and flowing through Srinagar and Wular Lake. 'Chenab' is wrong — it flows through the Jammu region (Doda, Kishtwar, Ramban). 'Indus' is wrong — it flows through Ladakh, not the Kashmir Valley. 'Ravi' is wrong — it originates in Himachal Pradesh and barely touches J&K.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about Wular Lake:

(i) It is the largest freshwater lake in India.
(ii) It is located in the Bandipora district of J&K.
(iii) The Jhelum River flows through Wular Lake.
(iv) It is a saltwater lake formed by tectonic activity.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — Wular Lake is the largest freshwater lake in India. (ii) is correct — it is in Bandipora district. (iii) is correct — the Jhelum River flows into and out of Wular Lake. (iv) is wrong — Wular is a freshwater lake, not a saltwater lake; it was formed by tectonic activity but remains freshwater.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The Chenab River originates from the confluence of which two rivers?
questions.explanation: The Chenab is formed by the confluence of the Chandra and Bhaga rivers at Tandi in Himachal Pradesh before entering J&K. 'Jhelum and Sindh' is wrong — Sindh is a tributary of the Jhelum in Kashmir. 'Lidder and Sind' is wrong — both are tributaries of the Jhelum. 'Tawi and Ravi' is wrong — Tawi is a tributary of the Chenab and Ravi is a separate river.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Dal Lake is one of the most famous lakes of J&K and a major tourist attraction.
Reason (R): Dal Lake is located in Srinagar and is known for its houseboats, shikaras, and the floating gardens called 'Rad'.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Assertion (A) is correct — Dal Lake is indeed one of J&K's most famous tourist destinations. Reason (R) is correct — it is in Srinagar and features houseboats, shikaras, and floating gardens (Rad). (R) explains (A) because these unique features are precisely what make Dal Lake a major attraction.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Match the following rivers of J&K with their regions:

Column I:
(a) Jhelum
(b) Chenab
(c) Tawi
(d) Indus

Column II:
(i) Flows through Jammu city
(ii) Flows through Kashmir Valley and Srinagar
(iii) Flows through Ladakh region
(iv) Flows through Doda, Kishtwar, and Ramban

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: Jhelum flows through the Kashmir Valley and Srinagar (ii). Chenab flows through Doda, Kishtwar, and Ramban (iv). Tawi flows through Jammu city (i). Indus flows through the Ladakh region (iii). The second option wrongly assigns Chenab to Kashmir Valley. The third option wrongly assigns Chenab to Jammu city. The fourth option wrongly assigns Jhelum to Ladakh.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The Jhelum River originates from which spring in J&K?
questions.explanation: The Jhelum River originates from the Verinag Spring in Anantnag district. 'Achabal Spring' is wrong — it is a famous Mughal garden spring that feeds into local streams, not the source of Jhelum. 'Chashme Shahi Spring' is wrong — it is a small spring near Srinagar. 'Kokernag Spring' is wrong — though it is one of the largest springs in Kashmir, it is not the origin of the Jhelum.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Which of the following are tributaries of the Jhelum River in the Kashmir Valley?

(i) Lidder (Liddar)
(ii) Sind (Sindh)
(iii) Vishav (Veshaw)
(iv) Chandra

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: Lidder (i), Sind (ii), and Vishav (iii) are all tributaries of the Jhelum in the Kashmir Valley. Chandra (iv) is wrong — Chandra is a tributary that forms the Chenab River (along with Bhaga) in Himachal Pradesh, not a tributary of the Jhelum.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about Pangong Tso Lake:

(i) It is situated in the Ladakh region at a very high altitude.
(ii) It is a saltwater lake.
(iii) Part of the lake extends into China (Tibet).
(iv) It is the largest freshwater lake in India.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — Pangong Tso is in Ladakh at about 4,350 m altitude. (ii) is correct — it is a saltwater (brackish) lake. (iii) is correct — about two-thirds of the lake lies in China. (iv) is wrong — Pangong is saltwater, not freshwater; the largest freshwater lake in India is Wular Lake.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The Tawi River is a major tributary of which river?
questions.explanation: The Tawi River, which flows through Jammu city, is a tributary of the Chenab River. 'Jhelum' is wrong — Tawi is in the Jammu region and joins the Chenab, not the Jhelum. 'Indus' is wrong — the Indus flows through Ladakh. 'Ravi' is wrong — Tawi flows into the Chenab, not the Ravi.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The rivers of J&K have significant hydroelectric potential.
Reason (R): The rivers flow through mountainous terrain with steep gradients, creating ideal conditions for generating hydroelectric power.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Assertion (A) is correct — J&K's rivers have enormous hydroelectric potential (estimated ~20,000 MW). Reason (R) is correct — steep gradients and high-volume flow create ideal conditions for hydropower. (R) explains (A) because the topographical conditions described are precisely what give these rivers their hydroelectric potential.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: Manasbal Lake, known as the 'Supreme Gem of all Kashmir Lakes', is located in which district?
questions.explanation: Manasbal Lake is located in Ganderbal district, about 30 km from Srinagar. It is known for its clear waters and lotus blooms. 'Srinagar' is wrong — Dal and Nigeen lakes are in Srinagar. 'Bandipora' is wrong — Wular Lake is in Bandipora. 'Anantnag' is wrong — Verinag Spring is in Anantnag, not Manasbal.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Match the following lakes with their key features:

Column I:
(a) Dal Lake
(b) Wular Lake
(c) Pangong Tso
(d) Manasbal Lake

Column II:
(i) Largest freshwater lake in India
(ii) Famous for houseboats and shikaras
(iii) High-altitude saltwater lake in Ladakh
(iv) Known as the 'Supreme Gem of Kashmir Lakes'

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: Dal Lake is famous for houseboats and shikaras (ii). Wular Lake is the largest freshwater lake in India (i). Pangong Tso is a high-altitude saltwater lake in Ladakh (iii). Manasbal is known as 'Supreme Gem of Kashmir Lakes' (iv). The second option wrongly assigns 'largest freshwater' to Dal. The third option wrongly assigns Pangong's description to Wular. The fourth option wrongly assigns 'Supreme Gem' to Dal.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The Sind (Sindh) River, a tributary of the Jhelum, flows through which famous valley?
questions.explanation: The Sind River flows through Sonamarg ('Meadow of Gold') in Ganderbal district. 'Lidder Valley' is wrong — the Lidder River flows through Pahalgam and the Lidder Valley. 'Gurez Valley' is wrong — the Kishanganga River flows through Gurez. 'Lolab Valley' is wrong — it is drained by the Lolab Nallah in Kupwara.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the Lidder River:

(i) It originates from the Kolahoi Glacier.
(ii) It flows through Pahalgam, a famous tourist destination.
(iii) It is a tributary of the Jhelum River.
(iv) It flows through the Ladakh region.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — the Lidder originates from the Kolahoi Glacier. (ii) is correct — it flows through Pahalgam. (iii) is correct — it joins the Jhelum near Anantnag. (iv) is wrong — the Lidder flows through the Kashmir Valley (Anantnag district), not Ladakh.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: Fill in the blank: The Nigeen Lake, often called the 'Jewel in the Ring', is located adjacent to __________ Lake in Srinagar.
questions.explanation: Nigeen Lake is a small, deep lake adjacent to Dal Lake in Srinagar, connected by a narrow waterway. 'Wular' is wrong — Wular is in Bandipora, far from Nigeen. 'Manasbal' is wrong — it is in Ganderbal district. 'Anchar' is wrong — while Anchar Lake is also near Srinagar, Nigeen is specifically adjacent to Dal Lake.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The Kishanganga River flows through which valley in J&K?
questions.explanation: The Kishanganga River (called Neelum in Pakistan) flows through the picturesque Gurez Valley in Bandipora district. 'Kashmir Valley' is wrong — the main river of Kashmir Valley is the Jhelum. 'Lidder Valley' is wrong — the Lidder River flows through that valley. 'Chenab Valley' is wrong — the Chenab is a separate river system.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Which of the following lakes are located in the Ladakh region?

(i) Pangong Tso
(ii) Tso Moriri
(iii) Tso Kar
(iv) Dal Lake

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: Pangong Tso (i), Tso Moriri (ii), and Tso Kar (iii) are all high-altitude lakes in the Ladakh region. Dal Lake (iv) is wrong — it is located in Srinagar in the Kashmir Valley, not in Ladakh.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Wular Lake faces environmental threats including shrinkage and pollution.
Reason (R): Encroachment, siltation from the Jhelum River, and growth of weeds have reduced the lake's area over decades.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Assertion (A) is correct — Wular Lake has been shrinking and facing pollution. Reason (R) is correct — encroachment, siltation, and weed growth are major factors. (R) explains (A) because these specific factors are the direct causes of the environmental threats to Wular Lake.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The Sheshnag Lake, located on the route to the Amarnath Cave, is famous for:
options: Being a glacial lake on the Amarnath Yatra pilgrimage route
Being the source of the Jhelum River
Being the largest lake in Ladakh
Having hot springs with medicinal properties
questions.correctAnswer: Being a glacial lake on the Amarnath Yatra pilgrimage route
questions.explanation: Sheshnag Lake is a beautiful glacial lake at about 3,590 m altitude on the traditional pilgrimage route to Amarnath Cave. 'Source of Jhelum' is wrong — the Jhelum originates from Verinag Spring. 'Largest lake in Ladakh' is wrong — Sheshnag is in the Kashmir Valley region, and Pangong is Ladakh's largest. 'Hot springs' is wrong — Sheshnag is a cold glacial lake.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about Tso Moriri Lake:

(i) It is located in the Changthang Plateau of Ladakh.
(ii) It is a high-altitude lake at over 4,500 metres.
(iii) It is designated as a Ramsar Wetland Site.
(iv) It is a freshwater lake used for irrigation in Srinagar.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — Tso Moriri is in the Changthang Plateau of Ladakh. (ii) is correct — it is at approximately 4,522 m elevation. (iii) is correct — it was designated a Ramsar Site in 2002. (iv) is wrong — Tso Moriri is a remote, high-altitude lake in Ladakh, not connected to irrigation in Srinagar.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The Anchar Lake in Srinagar is significant because:
options: It is the second largest lake in the Kashmir Valley after Wular
It is the deepest lake in India
It is a saltwater lake used for salt production
It was artificially created by the Mughal emperors
questions.correctAnswer: It is the second largest lake in the Kashmir Valley after Wular
questions.explanation: Anchar Lake is the second largest lake in the Kashmir Valley, located in Srinagar. 'Deepest lake in India' is wrong — that distinction does not belong to Anchar. 'Saltwater lake for salt production' is wrong — Anchar is a freshwater lake. 'Artificially created by Mughals' is wrong — it is a natural lake.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Match the following rivers with their origin/source:

Column I:
(a) Jhelum
(b) Chenab
(c) Lidder
(d) Kishanganga

Column II:
(i) Kolahoi Glacier
(ii) Verinag Spring
(iii) Confluence of Chandra and Bhaga
(iv) Krishansar and Vishansar Lakes (near Sonamarg)

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: Jhelum originates from Verinag Spring (ii). Chenab from the confluence of Chandra and Bhaga (iii). Lidder from Kolahoi Glacier (i). Kishanganga from Krishansar and Vishansar lakes area (iv). The second option wrongly assigns Chandra-Bhaga to Jhelum. The third option wrongly assigns Kolahoi to Chenab. The fourth option wrongly assigns Verinag to Kishanganga.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The Indus River enters J&K (Ladakh) from which direction?
options: From Himachal Pradesh in the south
questions.explanation: The Indus originates near Lake Mansarovar in Tibet and enters the Ladakh region of J&K from the south-east. 'Himachal Pradesh' is wrong — the Indus does not flow through HP. 'Pakistan' is wrong — the Indus flows from India into Pakistan, not the reverse. 'Afghanistan' is wrong — while the Indus basin touches Afghanistan via the Kabul River, the main Indus enters Ladakh from Tibet.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the Chenab River in J&K:

(i) It is the largest river of J&K by volume of water.
(ii) Major hydroelectric projects like Salal, Baglihar, and Dulhasti are built on it.
(iii) It flows through the districts of Doda, Kishtwar, and Ramban.
(iv) It originates within the Kashmir Valley near Srinagar.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — the Chenab is the largest river in J&K by water volume. (ii) is correct — Salal, Baglihar, and Dulhasti are all on the Chenab. (iii) is correct — it flows through these Jammu region districts. (iv) is wrong — the Chenab originates in Himachal Pradesh (Lahaul-Spiti), not in the Kashmir Valley.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The 'Floating Gardens' (locally called 'Rad') are a unique feature of which lake?
questions.explanation: The floating gardens (Rad) are a distinctive feature of Dal Lake in Srinagar, where vegetables are grown on floating beds of aquatic vegetation. 'Wular Lake' is wrong — while Wular has some floating vegetation, the famous Rad gardens are associated with Dal. 'Manasbal Lake' is wrong — it is known for lotus flowers, not floating gardens. 'Nigeen Lake' is wrong — it is smaller and does not have the Rad cultivation tradition.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: Fill in the blank: The Zanskar River, a major tributary of the __________, flows through the Zanskar region of Ladakh.
questions.explanation: The Zanskar River is a major left-bank tributary of the Indus River, joining it near Nimmu in Ladakh. 'Chenab' is wrong — the Chenab flows through the Jammu region. 'Jhelum' is wrong — the Jhelum is in the Kashmir Valley. 'Kishanganga' is wrong — it is a tributary of the Jhelum, not related to Zanskar.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Which of the following are Ramsar Wetland Sites in J&K/Ladakh?

(i) Wular Lake
(ii) Tso Moriri
(iii) Hokersar Wetland
(iv) Pangong Tso

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: Wular Lake (i), Tso Moriri (ii), and Hokersar Wetland (iii) are all designated Ramsar Sites. Pangong Tso (iv) is wrong — though it is ecologically important, it has not been designated as a Ramsar Site.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The Jhelum River is crucial for the agriculture of the Kashmir Valley.
Reason (R): The river and its tributaries provide water for irrigation of rice paddies and other crops throughout the valley floor.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Assertion (A) is correct — the Jhelum is vital for Kashmir's agriculture. Reason (R) is correct — its waters irrigate the valley's rice paddies and other crops. (R) explains (A) because the irrigation support is the direct reason the river is crucial for agriculture.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The Hokersar Wetland, an important bird sanctuary, is located near:
questions.explanation: Hokersar Wetland is located about 14 km north of Srinagar and serves as a habitat for migratory birds. 'Jammu' is wrong — Hokersar is in the Kashmir Valley. 'Leh' is wrong — it is in Ladakh, far from Hokersar. 'Kishtwar' is wrong — it is in the Chenab Valley region of Jammu.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the Vishav (Veshaw) River:

(i) It is a right-bank tributary of the Jhelum.
(ii) It flows through the Shopian and Pulwama districts.
(iii) It originates from the Pir Panjal range.
(iv) It flows through the Ladakh region.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — Vishav is a right-bank tributary of the Jhelum. (ii) is correct — it flows through Shopian and Pulwama. (iii) is correct — it originates from the Pir Panjal range. (iv) is wrong — Vishav is entirely in the Kashmir Valley, not in Ladakh.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The Tarsar and Marsar Lakes in J&K are famous for:
options: Being twin alpine lakes popular for trekking in the Aru Valley area
Being the source of the Chenab River
Being the largest lakes in Ladakh
Being artificial reservoirs built for irrigation
questions.correctAnswer: Being twin alpine lakes popular for trekking in the Aru Valley area
questions.explanation: Tarsar and Marsar are twin high-altitude alpine lakes in the Anantnag district, accessible through the Aru Valley, and are popular trekking destinations. 'Source of Chenab' is wrong — the Chenab originates from Chandra and Bhaga. 'Largest lakes in Ladakh' is wrong — they are in Kashmir, not Ladakh. 'Artificial reservoirs' is wrong — they are natural glacial lakes.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Match the following lakes with their districts:

Column I:
(a) Wular Lake
(b) Dal Lake
(c) Manasbal Lake
(d) Sheshnag Lake

Column II:
(i) Srinagar
(ii) Bandipora
(iii) Ganderbal
(iv) Anantnag

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: Wular Lake is in Bandipora (ii). Dal Lake is in Srinagar (i). Manasbal Lake is in Ganderbal (iii). Sheshnag Lake is in Anantnag district, on the Amarnath route (iv). The second option wrongly places Wular in Srinagar. The third option wrongly places Dal in Ganderbal. The fourth option wrongly places Manasbal in Anantnag.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The Dachigam National Park, which protects the catchment area of which water body, is crucial for Srinagar's water supply?
questions.explanation: Dachigam National Park protects the catchment area that feeds Dal Lake, ensuring clean water flows into the lake. 'Wular Lake' is wrong — Wular's catchment is in Bandipora, not Dachigam's area. 'Manasbal Lake' is wrong — it has a separate catchment in Ganderbal. 'Anchar Lake' is wrong — its water comes from different sources.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
The following data shows the approximate areas of major lakes in J&K:

Wular Lake → 160-260 (seasonal)
Dal Lake → 18
Pangong Tso → 700 (total, India+China)
Manasbal Lake → 3

Which lake has the largest area entirely within India?
questions.explanation: Wular Lake at 160-260 sq km (seasonally variable) is entirely within India and is the largest. Pangong Tso is larger overall (700 sq km) but only about one-third (roughly 230 sq km) lies in India, and that portion fluctuates — Wular at its maximum exceeds it. 'Dal Lake' is wrong — at 18 sq km it is much smaller. 'Manasbal Lake' is wrong — at 3 sq km it is the smallest listed.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the Indus River in J&K/Ladakh:

(i) It enters India in the Ladakh region.
(ii) The Zanskar River is its major tributary in Ladakh.
(iii) It flows from south-east to north-west through Ladakh.
(iv) It originates within the Kashmir Valley.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — the Indus enters India in Ladakh from Tibet. (ii) is correct — the Zanskar is a major tributary of the Indus in Ladakh. (iii) is correct — the Indus flows from SE to NW through Ladakh before entering Pakistan. (iv) is wrong — the Indus does not originate in or flow through the Kashmir Valley; it originates near Mansarovar in Tibet.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Which of the following rivers of J&K ultimately drain into the Arabian Sea?

(i) Jhelum
(ii) Chenab
(iii) Indus
(iv) All of the above (via the Indus system)

Select the correct option:
options: All of the above (via the Indus system)
questions.correctAnswer: All of the above (via the Indus system)
questions.explanation: The Jhelum, Chenab, and Indus are all part of the Indus river system, which ultimately drains into the Arabian Sea near Karachi, Pakistan. All rivers of J&K belong to the Indus system. '(i) and (ii) only' is wrong because the Indus itself also drains into the Arabian Sea. '(iii) only' is wrong because all three drain into the Arabian Sea. '(i) and (iii) only' is wrong because the Chenab also joins the system.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The Nagin (Nigeen) Lake is known for:
options: Being called the 'Jewel in the Ring' due to its ring of trees and its clear waters
Being the deepest lake in Asia
Being the only tidal lake in J&K
Having naturally hot water throughout the year
questions.correctAnswer: Being called the 'Jewel in the Ring' due to its ring of trees and its clear waters
questions.explanation: Nigeen Lake is called the 'Jewel in the Ring' because of the ring of trees (mostly chinar) surrounding it and its remarkably clear, deep waters. 'Deepest lake in Asia' is wrong — Nigeen is not even the deepest lake in J&K. 'Only tidal lake' is wrong — J&K has no tidal lakes as it is landlocked. 'Hot water' is wrong — Nigeen has cold freshwater.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
The following data shows the length of major rivers flowing through J&K:

Indus → 3,180, ~400
Jhelum → 725, ~400
Chenab → 960, ~500

Which river has the longest stretch within J&K territory?
questions.explanation: The Chenab flows approximately 500 km within J&K, making it the river with the longest stretch in the territory. 'Indus' is wrong — it flows about 400 km in J&K/Ladakh. 'Jhelum' is wrong — it flows about 400 km in J&K. 'All are equal' is wrong — the Chenab has a notably longer stretch.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about flood management in J&K:

(i) The Jhelum floods of September 2014 were among the worst in Kashmir's recent history.
(ii) Wular Lake acts as a natural flood absorption basin for the Jhelum.
(iii) Flood spill channels have been constructed to divert excess Jhelum water.
(iv) Flooding is impossible in the Kashmir Valley due to its mountainous terrain.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — the September 2014 Jhelum floods devastated Srinagar and surrounding areas. (ii) is correct — Wular Lake absorbs floodwaters from the Jhelum, acting as a natural reservoir. (iii) is correct — flood spill channels like the Flood Spill Channel have been built. (iv) is wrong — the Kashmir Valley is actually flood-prone because it is a flat basin surrounded by mountains with the Jhelum as the only outlet.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The Tso Kar Lake in Ladakh is notable because:
options: It is a high-altitude salt lake where salt was traditionally harvested
It is the source of the Jhelum River
It is India's only volcanic lake
It is connected to Dal Lake by an underground channel
questions.correctAnswer: It is a high-altitude salt lake where salt was traditionally harvested
questions.explanation: Tso Kar ('White Lake') is named for the white salt deposits on its shores; salt was historically harvested by the Changpa nomads. 'Source of Jhelum' is wrong — Jhelum originates from Verinag. 'Volcanic lake' is wrong — Tso Kar is a tectonic/endorheic lake. 'Connected to Dal Lake' is wrong — Tso Kar is in remote Ladakh, hundreds of kilometres from Dal Lake.
